subject: Landing-zone rebate structure & fallthrough adjudication — RetailOne
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@retailone.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: Taylor Chen <taylor.chen@retailone.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Landing-zone rebate structure & fallthrough — RetailOne

Jonas,

Thanks again for the call this morning. RetailOne's procurement team asked me to get a clearer picture of how Redwood would structure a landing-zone rebate for the initial migration from CloudServe — specifically:

- How the rebate phases against committed consumption (pilot -> ramp -> steady-state)
- What fallthrough protections you can offer if CloudServe reduces capacity mid-rollout
- Whether the rebate can be applied as a one-time migration credit or amortized across invoices

I've attached a high-level econ sheet we use internally to estimate migration uplift. Can you and your team confirm what realistic rebate buckets look like for a 12–18 month commercial relationship? Our commercial window is tight — we'd like terms to be included in a commercial letter by 10/27.

Thanks,

Liam O'Connor
Senior Procurement Manager
RetailOne
Attachments: RetailOne_Migration_Econ_Sheet.xlsx (xlsx - 36KB)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@retailone.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Landing-zone rebate structure & fallthrough — RetailOne

Hi Liam — appreciate the clarity and the econ sheet. Quick answers up front, then we can formalize:

1) Phasing: Pilot (0–3 months) — pilot credit to offset integration and benchmark work; Ramp (3–9 months) — tiered rebate tied to cumulative token consumption; Steady-state (9+ months) — ongoing discount off published consumption rates.

2) Fallthrough protections: We offer a two-track protection: guaranteed capacity SLA on Dedicated pools for a 3-month buffer, plus an emergency credit if CloudServe reduces capacity causing degraded throughput during the ramp. The emergency credit is calibrated to missed availability / SLA delta.

3) Credit application: We can amortize credits across invoices (typical for procurement) or provide a one-off migration credit. RetailOne preference?

I'll loop Marissa (commercial) and Karthik (solutions) to provide numbers and an ops-risk callout.

Next steps: Marissa will draft two alternatives (one weighted to up-front credit, one to amortized rebate) and Karthik will outline required handoffs and runbook items for a no-downtime migration. Can we book a 30-min sync Thursday 10/22?

Best,

Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
redwood.com | (650) 555-0142
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@retailone.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Landing-zone rebate structure & fallthrough — RetailOne

Liam, Jonas —

Attached is a short worksheet with two commercial structures:

A) Migration Credit (one-time): $350k credit applied in first invoice + 12% consumption discount during ramp months (months 3–9). Pros: simple accounting, fast to contract. Cons: less runway to prove value, credit impacts gross ARR recognition.

B) Amortized Rebate: $100k upfront credit + tiered rebate (5% -> 12% -> 18%) applied as a credit each month tied to usage thresholds. Pros: aligns incentives, preserves recognition; Cons: more complex invoicing.

Fallthrough policy (both structures): If CloudServe reduces capacity and RetailOne experiences >20% throughput degradation vs baseline during ramp, we trigger an emergency credit equal to 1 month's blended consumption at prior rates, plus priority routing to Dedicated pools for 30 days.

Karthik — any redlines on ops commitments?

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_proposal_v3.pdf (pdf - 275KB), commercial_structures_vRETAILONE.xlsx (xlsx - 48KB)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@retailone.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Landing-zone rebate structure & fallthrough — RetailOne

Quick ops note — from a migration risk and compatibility perspective:

- We estimate a 2–4 week validation window for prefix/KV cache behavior when switching from CloudServe models. During this window we recommend a staged cutover (10–25% traffic slices) to limit customer-visible regressions.
- Dedicated pool reservation required to guarantee throughput in the critical 30-day post-cutover window; that maps to the fallthrough protection Marissa outlined.
- If RetailOne prefers a one-time credit, we can increase the upfront credit by 15% to offset the additional ops risk we absorb.

Happy to join the Thursday sync to walk runbook milestones.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@retailone.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Landing-zone rebate structure & fallthrough — RetailOne

Team — thanks for the thorough options. RetailOne preference is the Amortized Rebate (Option B) — it fits our accounting and keeps both sides incentivized. Two asks before I push to legal:

1) Please confirm the exact monthly tier thresholds for the 5% -> 12% -> 18% ladder and an example invoice showing amortization.
2) Add a clause clarifying the emergency credit calculation (we want the formula documented so procurement can sign off).

If you can get that into a short commercial letter by end of day 10/27 we should be ready to move to legal. Also, can you include an ops-runbook appendix (even bullet points) that shows rollback criteria for the staged cutover?

I'll send a follow-up with the exact legal contact.

Appreciate it —
Liam
